summary:
1.5.1 gives the bottles to drink soon a page of their own, to sort and filter them.

The « To drink soon » banner of the wine list stays short: it keeps its counts, and unfolded it shows the eight most urgent bottles, then « See the N bottles », which opens the new « To drink » page. That page lists every bottle to drink soon, the most urgent first. Sort it by any column: urgency, peak year (the oldest first), vintage, colour, « drink before » or location. Filter it by urgency, by wine colour or by name, and switch between one row per bottle and one row per wine and vintage, with its number of bottles. Tick bottles to give them a « drink before », move them or change their status, or use the ⋯ menu of a bottle. The sort, filters and view stay when you reload the page or come back to it. An assistant connected through MCP can ask for the bottles to drink of one urgency or one colour, sorted by peak year.

1.5.0 shows which bottles to drink soon.

A bottle can now carry a date to drink it before: a year, or a month of a year. Set it in one click with « This month » or « This year », or choose a year and a month, on one bottle from its menu or on several ticked ones, from the bottle list of a wine or of a storage case; the bottle form has the field too. Without a date, the optimum year of the bottle takes over. The wine list opens with a banner of the bottles to drink soon: those whose date has passed, which stay flagged as late until you change or remove the date, then this month's, this year's, and those that reached their optimum year. It unfolds their list. A bottle drunk or taken out of the cellar leaves the list and keeps its date. On the storage page, a « Bottles to drink » button marks the cases that hold some; the preferences set how far ahead it looks and whether it is on when the page opens. The API, the exports and imports and the MCP tools follow: assistants can list the bottles to drink soon, find bottles by optimum year and set the date. Bottles from earlier versions have no date, and nothing needs doing to upgrade.

1.4.1 makes the buttons react visibly when the pointer is over them, in the light and the dark theme.

Every kind of button now follows one rule. A filled button, such as the number of bottles on a wine card, darkens in the light theme and lightens in the dark theme. A quiet button, such as the icons of a card, a table header or a storage case, takes the light background of the menus. The ring that shows the button reached with the keyboard is drawn in the full colour of the theme, links included. A disabled button no longer reacts. On the storage page, every container now gets the same neutral name pill: colour there tells the colour of the wines.

1.4.0 adds a list view of the wines next to the cards, gives each wine colour a real colour, shown on the storage page, in the statistics and on the wine cards, turns the storage page into a map of the cellar, and gives an AI assistant more to do and more context: it can take bottles out of the cellar, put them back and edit wines and bottles, and every refusal says exactly what is wrong.

My Wines can now show the wines as a list, one row per wine, next to the cards. On a computer, the list is a table with the photo, the wine with its producer and classification, the region, colour, vintage, price, bottles and rating; on a phone, each row gives the name, the producer and region, then the colour, vintage, bottles and price. Nothing is cut: a long name wraps and its row grows. A click anywhere on a row opens the wine; the bottles count, the bookmark, add a bottle and the ⋮ menu, with edit and duplicate, work as on a card, with the keyboard too, and on a phone the ⋮ menu holds every action. The Cards and List buttons next to Show images switch the view; the address of the page keeps that choice, so that coming back from a wine, reloading the page or sharing its link keeps the view. Preferences › Default Wine List View chooses the view the list opens in. Search, filters, sorting and the images switch work the same in both views.

Each wine colour now has a real colour. Rouge, Blanc, Rosé, Jaune and N/A start with a wine-like colour (deep red, pale gold, salmon, amber and grey), also when they were renamed to Red, White or Yellow; any other colour starts grey. Change a colour in Admin › Data › Wine Colors: the form shows a colour picker, and a badge with the name in the colour picked. A colour created from the wine form, or added in Admin › Data without picking one, gets the colour of its name, or grey for any other name. The storage page fills each bottle with the colour of its wine, the statistics draw the colour chart in these colours, the wine cards show the colour badge in its colour with a bar of that colour along their left edge, and the list view, the wine page and the bottle lists (out of the cellar, history, all the bottles of the storage page) show the coloured badge next to the wine. Each bottle of the storage page, each badge, each bar and each square of the statistics legend has a thin edge of its own colour, darker in the light theme and lighter in the dark theme, so that a pale white stays visible on a light background and a deep red on a dark one. Exports, imports and backups carry the colour; a file made by an earlier version gives each colour the one of its name.

An AI assistant connected to Cellar's MCP server can now do more, when you allow changes. It takes bottles out of the cellar and puts them back in a case, which also undoes a bottle marked drunk by mistake; changes a wine (target quantity, description, producer, appellation, grapes…) and the fields of bottles (price, value, vintage, optimum, purchase date, format, origin, barcode); changes the quantity or note of a wish; and deletes bottles added by mistake, a change Cellar marks as one that cannot be undone. With a read-only token too, it lists the bottles of the whole cellar by availability and by the day they were drunk or bought, to answer « what did we drink this month? ». Admin › Settings › MCP access says what each choice allows, deleting bottles included. README-Docker now explains that the Claude apps on the web and on a phone, and the connectors of the desktop app, call from the internet and cannot reach a Cellar on your home network: use Claude Code, or a client on your network that sends the token.

The storage page is now a map of the cellar. Click or tap a case, or reach it with the keyboard, to see the bottles it holds, with their wine, vintage and coloured badge; the name of a wine opens its page. The ⋮ menu of a bottle marks it drunk (with the date and a note), moves it, or opens the bottle form. Tick several bottles, then Move to… another case: the case list shows each case under its container with its free places, and greys the cases without room for them, so that a full case refuses the move and nothing moves. The case and the map update at once. The bottle dialog of a wine and the bulk barcode entry choose their case the same way. On a wine's page, Show in the cellar opens the storage page with the cases that hold the wine highlighted; Show all removes the highlight. An AI assistant can list what a case holds too, with list_bottles and the id of a case, and so can a script, with GET /api/storage-cases/{id}/bottles.

A bottle marked drunk now keeps the case it was in, without taking a place there, as a bottle out of the cellar already did: if it was marked drunk by mistake, putting it back in the cellar returns it to that case, or says the case is full. In the app, the bottle form of a drunk bottle names that case, and choosing Available selects it. The cases, the storage map, the free space and the wine page's Storage locations box count only the bottles in the cellar: that box no longer counts a bottle out of the cellar. Bottles drunk before 1.4.0 have no case left to go back to. For scripts, GET /api/bottles now gives a drunk bottle the storageCaseId of the case it left. The AI assistant gets more context too: when Cellar refuses a change, the assistant is told why and gets the full list of what caused the refusal, such as every bottle id it did not recognise; every tool description has been rewritten to say which tool provides the ids, which tool fits which request, and what cannot be undone; a bottle out of the cellar or drunk shows the case it left as formerLocation, never as its location; and the lists of bottles and wines can be read past their first 200 results with offset.

Two refusals now say exactly what is wrong, to an AI assistant and to scripts: a change refused because a case is full gives the id of the case next to its name, and a wine, bottle or wish that refers to something that does not exist (a format, an origin, a case…) names the field and the id it gave, so that the assistant knows which one to correct.

1.3.2 redesigns the wine cards of the wine list.

Each wine card is now laid out sideways, with a portrait photo on the left, and every card has the same size, with each detail always in the same place: the name, the producer and region, the badges, then the classification, vintage and price behind their icons, and two lines of description. A text too long for its line fades out, and scrolls to its end while you point at the card; on a touch screen, the name gets two lines. The bottles, add a bottle, the bookmark, edit and duplicate now sit in a bar at the bottom of the card. The list keeps cards wide enough to read and shows one column fewer when the window narrows, instead of squeezing them. Every button of the app now shows the hand pointer.

1.3.1 polishes the menu and the wishlist button of 1.3.0.

The sections of the menu sit a little further apart, and the red count or the dot of Purchases now stays in front when you point at the section next to it. The wishlist now shows a bookmark instead of a heart: empty when a wine is not on the list, filled when it is. The bookmark now shows the hand pointer and always changes when you point at it: on the photo of a wine card, or the placeholder of a wine without one, its disc takes the theme's colour, in dark mode too.

1.3.0 reorganises the menu into sections, lets you take and crop several photos of a wine, and adds a wishlist next to the wines to buy again.

A wine can now have several photos. The wine list shows its main photo; the wine page shows them all, adds one, makes another the main photo or deletes one. On a phone, "Take a photo" opens the camera, and "Choose a file" picks an image, on a computer too. Before a photo is sent, a preview turns and crops it; it is then shrunk to about 1,600 pixels on its longest side and sent as JPEG, without its metadata, such as the position where it was taken. Images already stored stay as they are, each the main photo of its wines. Backups and data exports keep every photo; the CSV files still name only the main photo of a wine. Scripts find the new photo routes in docs/API.md.

The menu now has four sections: Cellar (My Wines, Storage, Out of Cellar, History), Purchases, Statistics and Tools. Hovering a section, or reaching it with the keyboard, shows its pages, and a click opens its first one. Preferences, Admin and Logout are behind the gear. The shortage page is now Purchases › Shortage; its old address still leads there. Purchases shows the number of wines in shortage, and the wine list links to the bottles out of the cellar. On touch screens, the ☰ menu lists the sections, and on a phone, the app installed on the home screen has a tab bar at the bottom.

Purchases now opens on a wishlist, next to the shortage, each tab with its count. Add a wine of your cellar with the heart on its card or its page, or type a name on the wishlist: a wine of the cellar is suggested, and any other name becomes a wish of its own, with a photo of the label if you like. Each wish takes a quantity and a note. "Add bottle" on a wish opens the usual bottle form; on a wish typed by name, "Create the wine" opens the wine form with that name and photo, then goes on to its bottles. Once you have added bottles of a wine on the wishlist, from there or anywhere else, the app asks whether to take it off the list: nothing leaves it without your say. Purchases shows the number of wines in shortage in red, or else a dot while the wishlist has wishes. Backups and data exports keep the wishlist; the CSV files leave it out. Admin › Images names the wishes that use an image. Scripts find the wishlist routes in docs/API.md, and an AI assistant can read the wishlist and, when you allow changes, add or remove wishes.

The dependencies were reviewed again before this release. No package that the server installs in the Docker image had a newer fix published by 24 October, so the server keeps the packages and the Node.js 24.22.1 of 1.2.0. A few small libraries that the build puts into the pages, for dates and dialogs, and some development tools take their latest fixes. The dependency audit still lists the moderate minimatch advisory of 1.1.0: Cellar still never uses the part of the ZIP library that runs minimatch, and the fix, minimatch 11.0.1, is still too recent and not yet accepted by that library.

1.2.0 adds an MCP server to Cellar, so that an AI assistant on your network can read your cellar and, if you allow it, update it, and publishes an OpenAPI description of the API.

The MCP server has its own access token, made in Admin › Settings › MCP access: Cellar shows it once, keeps only its hash, and can replace or revoke it. The token is read-only unless you tick "Allow changes". It opens the MCP server only, never the pages, the API or the admin, and a restore keeps the token of your instance.

The HTTP API now has an OpenAPI 3.1 description, [docs/openapi.json](https://github.com/Lulu300/cellar/blob/main/docs/openapi.json), for tools that generate a client, test the API or show it: every route, its parameters, the fields its request body takes with their limits, and the error format. [docs/API.md](https://github.com/Lulu300/cellar/blob/main/docs/API.md) remains the full reference, with the fields of the answers.

Cellar also serves, at `/api/openapi.json`, the OpenAPI description of the version it runs, without a session like the other reads, so a tool can read the description that matches your server.

An AI assistant on your network can now read your cellar through the MCP server at `/mcp`: it finds wines, shows a wine with its bottles and where they are, finds a bottle by its barcode, and gives the statistics, the wines to buy again and the free space in storage. [README-Docker.md](https://github.com/Lulu300/cellar/blob/main/README-Docker.md#ai-assistants-mcp) shows how to set up Claude Code, a desktop app or a local-model client with the address and the token. It works on your local network or through a VPN only, not from an assistant that calls from the internet.

When you tick "Allow changes", the assistant can also update your cellar, as you would in the app: add a wine and its bottles, mark bottles drunk with the day and a note, move bottles to another case, and change the notes of bottles and the rating of a wine. It checks each change with the same rules as the app and never reaches the admin: backups, restore, wipe, imports and the access code stay in the app. With a read-only token, every change is refused with a message saying where to allow it, and during a restore or an import a change is refused until it ends.

Serving Cellar over HTTPS behind a reverse proxy is easier: [docs/reverse-proxy.md](https://github.com/Lulu300/cellar/blob/main/docs/reverse-proxy.md) gives configurations to copy for nginx, SWAG, Caddy and Traefik, each tested in front of Cellar, with the upload size that a restore or an import needs, the time limits, and what the MCP server at `/mcp` needs from the proxy. It also says what to set in Nginx Proxy Manager and the Synology reverse proxy.

A restore, a ZIP import or a batch of images that takes more than 5 minutes to upload, over slow Wi-Fi or a VPN, no longer fails with `408`: Cellar now gives an upload 30 minutes to arrive, enough for 500 MB at 0.3 MB/s. Behind a reverse proxy, the proxy's own time limits apply too: the Traefik example of [docs/reverse-proxy.md](https://github.com/Lulu300/cellar/blob/main/docs/reverse-proxy.md) gives Traefik 40 minutes, and nginx, SWAG and Caddy set no overall time limit on an upload.

1.1.0 makes Cellar easier to install and use: install steps in the README, a link to the API documentation, an app you can install on your phone, and fixes found after 1.0.0.

The README now gives the installation steps, with a compose file to copy. The README and the admin page link to the API documentation.

Cellar installs on the home screen of a phone or a computer, with its new logo, a wine glass, and opens full screen like an app: on Android and on a computer, the browser offers to install it when Cellar is served over HTTPS; on an iPhone or iPad, use Share › Add to Home Screen. [Install on a phone](https://github.com/Lulu300/cellar/blob/main/README-Docker.md#install-on-a-phone) gives the steps. The glass also replaces the icon of the browser tab and of the header, and the browser bar takes the color of the header, in light and dark mode.

Every answer of the server, the static files such as the icons and the error pages included, now forbids other sites to show Cellar in a frame. In 1.0.0, only the pages, the API and the images did.

The backup messages are clearer: a backup or an export named "auto" is refused with a message saying that this name is kept for automatic backups and exports; downloading a backup deleted in the meantime says so and updates the list; and when the session expires while the backup of the previous data downloads, the login dialog keeps saying why it opened.

Names, producers, label preset descriptions, grape varieties and case suffixes are now measured like notes and descriptions, in the units that the forms count: an emoji counts as two characters, so 250 emoji fill the 500 characters of a name. The API, the forms and the CSV import now accept or refuse such a text the same way. A name that 1.0.0 accepted with many emoji can be too long now: your data keeps it, and exports, backups and restores keep it whole, but you have to shorten it before you can save the wine, container, label preset, country, region or other reference that holds it again. Importing an export cuts such a name to its limit, as it already cuts notes and descriptions that are too long; the CSV import lists its row as invalid in the report.

The admin pages name each action once, from its button to its dialog and its message: the two "Edit" buttons of the settings now say what they change, Full Backup and Full Export keep their names in their dialogs and messages, an export of the backup list is no longer called a backup, the filters have their own "Clear Filters" button, the selected images are exported with "Export Selected", and on most phones the long titles of the admin dialogs no longer run under their close button.

A greyed button now says why: the login, the access code change, the label presets and the name of a new item added from a list show what is missing under the field or by the button. In the statistics, a tap on a bar shows its whole name and its number of bottles under the chart, so a name cut under its bar can be read on a phone too.

On a phone, the last long dialogs now keep their title and their buttons in view and scroll in between: the bottles of a wine, all the bottles of the storage page, the label presets, the bulk entry of barcodes, and the wipe and restore confirmations, which no longer run off a narrow screen in French. These dialogs and the long dialogs of the admin pages now fit in the height that the address bar of the phone leaves.

More greyed buttons now say why: adding or editing a country, region or other reference of the admin, renaming an image and the CSV import show what is missing, and the session timeout says which values it accepts. Changing the access code and saving a label preset show that they are under way, and a double click no longer sends them twice. When a list such as the country of a wine is filled from its appellation, the Cancel button of a new item typed in it stays usable.

The dependencies were reviewed again before this release. No package of the Docker image had a newer fix published by 24 October, so the image keeps the packages and the Node.js 24.22.1 of 1.0.0. The dependency audit lists one moderate advisory, in minimatch, which comes with the library that writes ZIP files: Cellar never uses the part of that library that runs minimatch, and the fix, in minimatch 11.0.1, is too recent and that library does not accept it yet.

In all the bottles of the storage page, the page numbers now stay in view under the list while it scrolls, so you no longer have to scroll to the end of the list to change page.

1.0.0 is the first public release of Cellar, a self-hosted manager for a home wine cellar. It runs as a Docker container, for example on a NAS, and is meant for a home network or a VPN: do not expose it directly to the Internet.

Cellar keeps your wines and their bottles: producer, appellation, vintage, format, drinking year, purchase price and value, and the case of the container where each bottle sits. Search and filter the cellar, find a bottle by its barcode, mark bottles consumed or out of the cellar, and see the history, the statistics and the wines that run short. Print barcode labels on PDF sheets, and scan codes with the device camera to find, consume or move bottles. In the admin pages, you back up the database and the images, on demand or on a schedule, restore them, import and export the data as CSV or as a ZIP with the images, and manage the reference lists and the images. The interface is in English and French, with light and dark modes and several color schemes.

To install it, pull the image `ghcr.io/lulu300/cellar` (tags `latest`, `1.0.0` and `1.0`, for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`), which needs no login, with the `docker-compose.yml` of this release: [README-Docker.md](https://github.com/Lulu300/cellar/blob/main/README-Docker.md) gives the steps, and how to build the image from source instead. Set `ORIGIN` to the exact URL you open Cellar at: the app refuses changes sent from any other address. On first start, choose an access code with the setup token that the container's logs print: anyone on the network can browse the cellar, and changes and the admin need the code.

Good to know:

- Cellar cannot be shown inside a frame, such as one on a NAS dashboard: open it with a link instead.
- Notes and wine descriptions hold up to 5,000 characters, counted as browsers count them, so an emoji takes two or more. The forms stop at 5,000 and the API refuses a longer text; CSV Import and Import from Export cut it to 5,000.
- The browser gives the scanner the camera only over HTTPS or on `localhost`: at an address such as `http://192.168.1.20:3005`, type or paste the codes, or serve Cellar over HTTPS behind a reverse proxy ([Scanner camera](https://github.com/Lulu300/cellar/blob/main/README-Docker.md#scanner-camera)).
- The names of countries, regions, appellations and the other reference lists are compared without their case: adding one under a name that another already has, in any case, gives that one, and renaming one to such a name is refused. An entry can still change the case of its own name.
- Importing a ZIP of images reads it into memory, and can take up to 5 times its size: on a NAS with little memory, import the images in several smaller ZIPs.
- Your own scripts can use the HTTP API of the app, which [docs/API.md](https://github.com/Lulu300/cellar/blob/main/docs/API.md) describes.

Report a problem or ask a question in the [issues](https://github.com/Lulu300/cellar/issues), with the version that the admin page shows, what you did and what you saw, and the lines of `docker compose logs cellar` around it. Never post your access code, setup token, cron token or backups: they give access to your cellar.
